questions.q: What is media, and why is an independent media important in a democracy?
answer: Media are the means of communicating with a large number of people at once, and mass media include newspapers, radio, television, films and the internet.

answer.text: In a democracy, media inform citizens about events and issues and help shape public opinion, allowing people to make informed choices. Media also act as a watchdog, exposing wrongdoing and holding the powerful to account.

To play these roles honestly, media must be independent — free from excessive control by the government or by business interests. Since media are funded largely through advertisements, owners and advertisers can influence what is shown, so an independent, balanced media is essential for citizens to receive fair and truthful information.

questions.q: Why should citizens read and watch the media critically?
answer: Although media inform us, they do not always give a complete or unbiased picture, so they must be approached critically.

answer.text: Media depend on advertisements and on their owners for funds, so business or political interests can shape which stories are covered and how.
Reporting can sometimes be sensational or one-sided, highlighting only part of a story to attract attention.

Good reporting should be balanced, factual and fair, showing different sides. Citizens should therefore compare several sources before forming an opinion, and value local and community media that give voice to ordinary people.
